chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Haroun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic, 'God will not seize you for what is vain in your oaths' [2:225]: 'The vain is the speech of the man who says, "No, by God" and "Yes, by God", and it is not binding upon anything.'

key_terms.أَيْمَان: Oaths/pledges — formal swearing by God's name
key_terms.اللَّغْوُ: Vain/idle speech — oaths uttered casually or habitually without binding intent
key_terms.يَعْقِدُ: To bind/contract — the notion of a legally enforceable oath

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about vain oaths (laghw al-yamin) in Quran 2:225?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides an authoritative interpretation of Quran 2:225, explaining that 'laghw' (vain speech) in oaths refers to casual, habitual utterances like 'No, by God' or 'Yes, by God' used in everyday conversation without genuine intent. Such informal oaths carry no legal weight and are not enforceable, distinguishing them from deliberate, binding oaths that carry jurisprudential consequences. This clarification was important for the early Muslim community who frequently used oath-expressions colloquially.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I heard himasws saying regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:225] Allah will not Seize you for what is vain in your oaths: ‘The vain is the speech of the man, ‘No, by Allahazwj’, and ‘Yes, by Allahazwj’, and it is not binding upon anything’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has narrated the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, about the meaning of the words of Allah, ‘. . . Allah will not hold you responsible for your meaningless oaths.’ [2:225]
Al-Laghw, (meaningless) is a reference to a man’s saying, ‘La wa Allah, (No, by Allah) Bala waAllah-i, (yes, by Allah)’ and it does not make anything binding.”
